# Noisy motif translations

For a noisy grid with one distinctive single-color seed motif amid zeros and another background color, record the motif's colored-cell offsets from its bounding box. Search for translated copies whose motif positions all contain zeros, recoloring those matching positions with the motif color. Preserve every other cell, including the original motif and zeros/background at non-motif positions inside the bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation: test motif translations when the grid visually consists of noisy background plus one seed object. Use demonstrations to validate the seed shape, legal translations within bounds, and any rotation/reflection; allow rotation or reflection only when the examples support it.

# Separator tile classification

When full-width and full-height separator lines partition a grid into equal tiles and output dimensions match the tile layout, map each tile to one output cell. Use demonstrations to identify the in-tile feature or count that determines that cell; do not assume every unusual cell or a lone marker is positive. For the pattern with color-8 separators, 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, output 1 for a tile with at least two 2s and 3 otherwise. Check the inferred rule against every demo.

# Diagonal periodic stripes

For sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field, identify the invariant of their parallel lines: constant row−column for down-right diagonals, or row+column for down-left diagonals. Demos may indicate that the output fills the whole grid with a periodic color sequence indexed by that invariant. Use zero-based row/column coordinates and verify the sign convention against observed output: for down-right stripes, `column−row` indexes phase; for down-left stripes, `row+column` does.

Infer the smallest plausible period and color per phase by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue. Use demonstrated outputs to establish the complete mapping when available; marker positions alone may not determine every residue's color. Color every cell from its phase, not just the sparse markers. Verify several cells against each demonstrated line and confirm the candidate reproduces every demo.

# Edge continuation

When demonstrations show color 1 marking an absent continuation at a grid edge, compare repeated rows, bands, or motif copies to infer the expected continuation and affected cells. It may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions. Color only confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Check changed and unchanged cells against every demo, and select repeated copies from that evidence—not from rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
